gaps.term: step: n(lg n)^(1-κ) is o(n log n)
gaps.quote: Since $(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}/\lg n = (\lg n)^{-\kappa} \to 0$, this running time is $o(n\log n)$
gaps.note: The page divides by lg n and concludes o(n log n), but it never says how the logarithm in n log n relates to lg n (the base of log is not stated, and the two differ only by a constant factor). It also never states that o(g) means the ratio tends to 0. The reader cannot check that the running time is o(n log n) from what the page gives.
